newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 12.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 12.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** India's Hindu nationalists said on Sunday they were gearing up to strengthen the party organisation ahead of a general election they expect later this year.
"We have alerted all the party units to be prepared for polls in 1997," Lal Krishan Advani, president of the rightwing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), told reporters.

** The Indian rupee opened steady against the dollar on Monday at 35.84/85. Dealers await the week's trends amid conflicting signals of enhanced dollar supply and suppressed dollar demand and external repayments beginning this week.
** Jittery investors are likely to put the brakes on a boom in Indian blue chips this week, but underlying sentiment is still bullish, dealers and analysts said at the weekend.
Dealers said liquidity was improving as retail investors, long equity-shy, were making commitments to pick up small capitalisation stocks.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top 30-share index rallied 154.26 points or 4.7 percent to end at 3,418.32 in the week to Friday -- up nearly 11 percent since the close of 1996.
